Senses.Explanation: A physical stick, cudgel, or staff, characteristically handled in public encounters and remembered as a house device. Its object grammar is explicit: Linji Yixuan picks one up and offers it to an interlocutor, Zhaozhou Congshen grabs one and warns against striking people wrongly, and Guizong Zhichang drives people out with one. In the Patriarchs' Hall Collection, Yantou Quanhuo calls Deshan Xuanjian's implement “the single white staff before his eyes.” Zhongfeng Mingben pairs “Linji's shout” with “Deshan's staff,” Nanyuan Huiyong picks up the staff before saying “under the staff, the forbearance of no-arising; meeting the occasion, one does not defer to his instructor,” and the fixed compound “staff and shout” joins it to the shout (喝). This object is not the same lexical thing as a held or planted walking staff (拄杖), and it is not the countable act of hitting recorded in the second sense.
Senses.Note: Object sense confirmed by pickup, transfer, attempted receipt, grasping, color, and instrumental “drive out” syntax (趁). Cross-check: “staff and shout” (棒喝) has its own entry and pairs the staff/blow family with the shout without erasing this split. No “bamboo strip” entry (竹篦) exists in the current termbase. Corpus inspection shows the bamboo strip (竹篦) as an object that can be raised, thrown down, and used to strike; one late line even says “give one blow with the bamboo strip” (打一竹篦). That family needs its own item-8 audit before any inference from the staff (棒) is copied to it. The present headword split is independently proved by its own grammar.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師拈棒與僧，其僧擬接，師便打。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Tiansheng Expanded Lamp Record (天聖廣燈錄), section on Linji Yixuan, records Linji picking up the staff, offering it, and striking when the interlocutor nearly receives it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 臨濟喝。德山棒。天皇餅。趙州茶。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Extensive Record of Tianmu Zhongfeng (天目中峰廣錄) records Zhongfeng Mingben's house-device list placing Deshan's staff beside Linji's shout, Tianhuang's cake, and Zhaozhou's tea.

Occurrences.Kwic: 南院拈棒云棒下無生忍臨機不讓師
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in its raised Nanyuan Huiyong saying, records Nanyuan picking up the staff and speaking of the forbearance of no-arising under it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 州捉住棒曰。已後莫錯打人去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Nanquan Puyuan, records Zhaozhou Congshen physically grabbing the staff and saying not to strike people wrongly later.

Occurrences.Kwic: 德山老漢只憑目前一個白棒
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), in Yantou Quanhuo's section, records Yantou saying that Deshan Xuanjian relies on the single white staff before him. Yantou is the exact speaker; Deshan is the person discussed.
The Jingde Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), section on Guizong Zhichang, records Guizong using the staff instrumentally to drive the interlocutor down and away.

Occurrences.Kwic: 至于祖師門下，棒喝交馳，龍象蹴踏，拈鎚豎拂，擎叉輥毬
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Record of Chan Master Juelang Daosheng of Tianjie (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄) records Juelang Daosheng listing “staff and shout” (棒喝) among lineage-gate actions. This anchors the longer family term without counting it toward standalone depth.

The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Ruibai (入就瑞白禪師語錄) records Ruibai Mingxue striking once with a bamboo strip (打一竹篦). This contrast row anchors the bamboo-strip control without treating its object/action behavior as standalone evidence for the headword.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師拈拄杖打，麻谷接却，相捉入方丈。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Record of Linji Yixuan (鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄) records Linji Yixuan picking up a walking staff (拄杖) to strike Magu. This anchors the distinct walking-staff control without making it evidence for standalone (棒).

Senses.Explanation: A countable act of striking, not the wooden object. The grammar proves the split: the corpus assigns one blow to one welt, gives Manjusri and Samantabhadra twenty blows each, gives thirty blows whether a person can speak or cannot, speaks of eating or deserving a blow, qualifies Linji's three encounters as painful blows, and calls a requested beating “one bout of blows.” Xuefeng's report that under Deshan's blows it was like a bucket-bottom falling out preserves a named case deployment. None of these can mean one, twenty, or thirty physical staffs. Zen records use the stroke as answer, penalty, test, appraisal, and later case label; the entry reports those uses without claiming a single result for every blow.
Senses.Note: Allowlist counts recorded in the audit: the headword “staff/blow” (棒), 18,109 hits in 415 texts; “one blow” (一棒), 2,954; “thirty blows” (三十棒), 2,766; “twenty blows” (二十棒), 407; “one bout of blows” (一頓棒), 63; “receive a blow” (喫棒), 1,191; and “painful blows” (痛棒), 752. The object-versus-blow split is preserved and strengthened: six object witnesses and seven act witnesses, with every sense independently anchored. The linked verse collection assigns the thirty-blows formula to Deshan Xuanjian; other witnesses must still be adjudicated rather than assumed identical.

Occurrences.Kwic: 德山示眾曰道得也三十棒道不得也三十棒
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked Collection of Chan Lineage Verse Comments on Old Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集) explicitly raises Deshan Xuanjian's formula assigning thirty blows whether one can speak or cannot.

The Patriarchs' Hall Collection (祖堂集), section on Baoci Guangyun, records Baoci asking whether someone deserves to receive a blow, using ‘eat a blow’ for undergoing the stroke. Baoci Guangyun is not yet on the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 我當時在德山棒下。如桶底脫相似。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), in Yuanwu Keqin's commentary, quotes Xuefeng Yicun reporting that under Deshan's blows it was like a bucket bottom falling away. The first-person quotation makes Xuefeng the speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 臨濟三遭痛棒，高安灘上知歸
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Ying'an Tanhua (應菴曇華禪師語錄) records Ying'an Tanhua's hall address counting and qualifying Linji's three encounters as painful blows.

Occurrences.Kwic: 文殊．普賢昨夜三更相打。每人與二十棒。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), section on Nanquan Puyuan, records Nanquan saying that Manjusri and Samantabhadra fought and were each given twenty blows.

The Blue Cliff Record (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄), in Zhou Chi's named preface, coordinates one blow with one welt and states the comparison's intended function. Zhou Chi is a lay preface author, not a Chan master, and is not on the master roster; his name is retained rather than falsely attributing his sentence to Yuanwu Keqin.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如今更思得一頓棒喫誰人為我行得
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), section on Linji Yixuan, records Linji wanting to receive one bout of blows and asking who can carry it out.
